maya: Quick share — ran a regional sweep for fenrir-7B-qlora (quantized) focusing on continuous-batching + scheduler fairness. Results look weird: eu-west h100 is slower than us-east a100 when max_batch_tokens > 4096. Anyone seen an inversion like this?

sam: can you paste the exact run command and kernel flags you used? :eyes:

maya: sure — command + flags I used:
```bash
./run_eval.sh --model fenrir-7b-qlora --quant q4_0 --max_batch_tokens 8192 --batch_window_ms 12 --kernel=auto --region=eu-west-1 --ctb_tilt=0.5 --fairshare=false
```
results (single-worker pool warm):
- eu-west-1 (h100, auto-kernel): p50 45ms p95 120ms throughput 270 rps
- us-east-1 (a100, auto-kernel): p50 38ms p95 95ms throughput 320 rps
I also tried 4096 and below — parity there, inversion only after 4096.

leo: are you running with KV-cache warmup enabled? distribution of seq lengths? sometimes seq tail triggers a different kernel path.

maya: KV-cache warmup = default (enabled). seq dist skewed — ~30% long requests > 2k tokens in eu test set, us test set was more uniform.

anu: my hunch: `--kernel=auto` sometimes picks the wrong flash-attn/tiling routine under high max_batch_tokens + skewed seq distribution on H100. Try forcing flash-attn-v2 or a tiling kernel override. On H100 auto can pick a fallback kernel that's worse for large batches.

infra-bot: deploy-log: kernel-picker patch v2.1 rolled to eu-west H100 pool at 2026-11-02T16:04Z (triggered by #eng-ml).

kai: can you run a small microbenchmark to confirm? e.g.
```bash
./bench_micro.sh --model fenrir-7b-qlora --quant q4_0 --max_batch_tokens 4096 --kernel=flash-attn-v2 --warmup=false --region=eu-west-1
./bench_micro.sh --model fenrir-7b-qlora --quant q4_0 --max_batch_tokens 8192 --kernel=flash-attn-v2 --warmup=false --region=eu-west-1
```
That isolates kernel behavior vs warmup/cache effects.

maya: ran that now. forcing `flash-attn-v2` on eu-west H100:
- max_batch_tokens=4096 -> p95 92ms throughput 330 rps
- max_batch_tokens=8192 -> p95 88ms throughput 340 rps
So forcing flash-attn-v2 eliminates the inversion and eu matches (slightly better) than a100 baseline. :thumbsup:

maya: additional note — q4_0 quant caused a tiny quality drift: ~0.6% drop on rouge-L vs fp16 on our eval set. Will run q4_1 and rerun evals. No large regressions but flagging for the model card.

sam: nice find. can you open an eval run linking the exact prompt set and add kernel override to the model onboarding checklist (temporary heuristic: prefer flash-attn-v2 on H100 when max_batch_tokens > 4096 and seq_tail_ratio > 0.25)?

maya: opened ticket #INFR-1284 with eval artifacts and a short plot (attached). will also push a shortpatch to the kernel-picker heuristic.

leo: also add a note in the rollout: when we switch quant variants (q4_0 -> q4_1) we should run the same kernel sweep and a fairness pass across regions (ctb tilt 0/0.5/0.8) so we don't regress tail latencies.

sam: agreed — I'll add that to the onboarding playbook. good work catching the kernel pick.

maya: thanks all. will follow up with q4_1 numbers tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
